nonblocking_findings.title: Retirement ends direct binary replay of the historical M0 probes
nonblocking_findings.detail: The 24 historical engineering probes are intentionally deleted without a new binary backup. Their original M0 receipts and accepted final models remain, and current F3 verification is unaffected. Preserve the stated historical replay limitation in the retirement receipt and later publication; do not represent these old M0 binaries as still available. This is a disclosed consequence of the requested storage plan, not a reason to expand the deletion set or add a substitute checkpoint.

checks.title: Original failure and six complete trainings are supported by primary evidence
checks.detail: All six full training receipts have BEST_OFFICIAL_MAP_TRAINING_COMPLETE and ordered epochs 1 through 50. Their step/batch counts are 2649/6559/1000 for each variant (20416 total), with matching epoch/batch pairs. Eleven of twelve parent jobs completed with exit0; original full metric_raw RGBNT100 remains FAILED/exit1, parent FAILED/report_invocations0. Its child contains only train COMPLETE/exit0. The traceback points to the original 10 GiB guard before creation of evaluate.log or an evaluation job; missing official_metrics/official_distances are recorded by the intake. This means first standalone strict reload evaluation, not absence of the fifty per-epoch evaluations.

checks.title: Retirement is limited to 24 closed engineering probe files
checks.detail: The exact list comprises 12 visual-update, 6 clean-public and 6 F2 m0_reload_probe.pth files, 8444122668 bytes. Three directly read completed reports contain 12/6/6 VERIFIED_COMPLETE rows; all 24 directly read historical training receipts are M0_PASS and record the listed probe SHA. Inventory sizes and recorded hashes match all candidates. Candidate paths are unique, under the trained-model root and disjoint from 24 protected final-best files and all 23 extant F3 binaries. Preparation derives the preflight exceptions from the actual completed rows. Runtime retirement checks owner process names, each terminal owner campaign and absent controller PID; resolves each candidate strictly, rejects symlinks and noncanonical paths, checks exact size/SHA and receipt, and verifies protected/public/source hashes before any unlink. Only those 24 individual files are unlinked; no directory, dataset, author/public weight or best checkpoint is a deletion target. Actual remote byte equality and process absence remain runtime gates.

checks.detail: The F3 source chain reads prior manifests and source bytes, not prior M0 weights. The unmodified verifier resolves M0 probes under the current F3 campaign name, whose six probes remain protected. The report reads only retained F2 normalized training_batch_order.jsonl files for historical parity; all three are currently byte-equal to both fresh F3 variants. The current evaluation loads public CLIP for the original reconstruction check and then the existing current F3 best_map.pth. No retired old probe appears in this evaluate/verify/report call path.

checks.title: The missing evaluation preserves the selected checkpoint and original scientific path
checks.detail: The helper obtains the exact original evaluate command from panel.command; launcher uses the original tri_reid interpreter. Dataset RGBNT100, recipe metric_raw, seed42, epochs50, initialization witness, training-feature protocol and output directory are unchanged. The helper only invokes evaluate, never prepare, m0 or train. run_metric.configure applies the same original in-memory foundation function bindings; f2 captured original_build_core before that replacement, so no recursion or substitute implementation is introduced. The evaluator reconstructs the original model, checks the original witness, strictly loads existing best_map.pth, verifies original latest-tie mAP-best epoch48 and saved metrics, and retains the less-than-1e-5 checks. It does not change training AMP, coefficients, checkpoint selection, seed, data scope or tolerance; the original standalone evaluator itself uses inference_mode without a new autocast override.

checks.title: Sealed source and original failure provenance remain separately attributable
checks.detail: All 265 source files and all 103 intake text files match their recorded size/hash; FINISH_SPEC, retirement spec and the original manifest agree on source265. All nine initialization/pair receipt hashes match. F2 source259 and the F1 predecessor source249 chain also match under the already-defined canonical protocol rule. The new helper and launcher are separate files outside source265. Before changing live child/parent JSON, the helper archives the original parent, child and failure log. After actual evaluation exit0 and verification it retains the original failed parent job as original_failure, records completion_provenance and changes the aggregate job PID to the finish controller. Original failed parent and child hashes and a separate finish STATUS distinguish this completion from the original worker exit1; the original worker log is not rewritten. Standard-library in-memory JSON checks confirmed the selected dictionary/list aliases update the intended entries and the saved original_failure retains exit1/PID2762610. These synthetic checks were not runtime evidence.

checks.title: Exactly one report attempt follows all six strict acceptances
checks.detail: The helper first awaits actual evaluator termination, records its return code and asserts zero, then calls the original verifier for the repaired endpoint and all six formal endpoints. The original verifier checks current M0 receipts, full50, selected epoch, strict metric parity, protocol/checkpoint/distance bindings and upstream parity. Only then is accepted_matrix written and parent aggregate status advanced to COMPLETE/report_invocations1, exactly as the original queue expects. The unchanged report requires all12 accepted jobs and all6 matrix rows, re-verifies each row, and checks original step/batch histories and retained F2 batch bytes before CPU saved-distance diagnosis. The existing report accepts the extra provenance fields. One subprocess.run calls it with CUDA hidden, and report_exit_code is written only after the actual return. finish-directory, original-parent-hash, absent result/report/log and exclusive-open guards prevent a repeat invocation through this same helper. COMPLETE alone is the existing pre-report aggregate state; terminal success additionally requires report_exit_code0 and finish ALL6_STRICT_AND_FIRST_REPORT_COMPLETE.

checks.title: The reviewed transport is restricted to 2026 GPU1 and preserves the original capacity gate
checks.detail: The added launcher requires this actual same-family/provisional no-blocker review and bound retirement/finish script hashes, the exact retired24 receipt, the original failed parent SHA, absent finish directory and free disk >=10737418240 bytes. It connects only to port2026 and checks GPU1 used memory <500 MiB before launching exactly one finish process with --gpu 1 in the original environment. The helper checks capacity again and sets CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to that physical index. The report runs with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES empty. There is no process kill, preemption, new 2025 execution or retraining. The inventory had GPU1 60 MiB and 4519247872 free bytes; adding the candidate byte count yields a projected 12963370540 bytes, but those old observations are not substituted for the live checks.

checks.title: Official query/gallery scope and label use are unchanged
checks.detail: The original evaluation path extracts all protocol query and gallery records with evaluation loaders, enforces full 1536-dimensional output counts and computes actual identity/camera or scene filtered scores. Checked protocol sizes are RGBNT201 836/836, RGBNT100 1715/8575, MSVR310 591/1055; MSVR retains 103 gallery-only identities. The evaluator uses original identity labels only for the metric/filter, not optimizer steps; inference receives images/camera ids. This review did not execute any scoring function or claim independent numerical runtime parity.
